name: Lightbox
summary: Modal image viewer contract with open state, content, image, close, previous and next navigation, counter, caption, focus trapping, and gallery keyboard behavior.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Fixed full-screen overlay that owns backdrop and visibility state.

anatomy.name: nav
anatomy.description: Previous or next image navigation control.

states.name: open
states.description: Visible overlay state controlled by lightbox--open.

behavior.name: visibility
behavior.description: The lightbox is hidden by default and becomes visible when lightbox--open is applied.

behavior.name: modalSemantics
behavior.description: The lightbox inherits modal dialog semantics and must describe the current image or gallery context.

behavior.name: focusManagement
behavior.description: Focus should move into the lightbox on open, remain contained while open, and return to the invoking element on close.

behavior.name: dismissal
behavior.description: The lightbox should close on Escape, explicit close, or documented backdrop interaction.

behavior.name: galleryNavigation
behavior.description: Previous and next controls should update the image, counter, caption, and accessible description together.

properties.name: open
properties.description: Controls whether the lightbox overlay is visible; focus management and dismissal remain target behavior.

properties.name: alt
properties.description: Accessible alternative text for the displayed image.

properties.name: caption
properties.description: Optional visible caption synchronized with the displayed image.

accessibility: Trap focus inside the lightbox while it is open and restore focus to the invoking element on close.
Close on Escape and provide a visible close control.
Provide descriptive alt text for every image.
Keep counter, caption, and accessible description synchronized when navigating images.
Respect reduced motion preferences for image transitions.

web.notes: Implemented by class composition in components/css/layout.css; modal behavior, focus trapping, image navigation, and state synchronization must be provided by the consuming target.
